item.content:encoded:
I wonder what it says about me that I could see the ending coming a mile away.
Anyway I'm on the fence about whether or not the ethics committee would see this as needlessly cruel. Sure the Foundation should be able to find a sufficient amount of doctors that meet the requirements without too much trouble, but is it more ethical to subject the same person (or whatever minimum number) to this repeating psychological torture with no lasting memory, or to subject more doctors to the same experience, but only once rather than indefinitely?
I can't really say how they'd handle it because I can't figure out that conundrum myself. No vote, at least for now.

I would think the helmets less necessary following the amnestic revision to the procedure. If she's getting dosed once a week, there's no worry about her making long-term identifications. If anything, the dread on realizing it's the SAME group of psychos near the end of the cycle should make the process more intense.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Waaaayyyyyy late to this question, but maybe it'll be interesting to some other curious person — pharmicists apparently don't, they take something similar, but not the Hippocratic Oath. It came up while discussing the death penalty with a pharmicist friend — they could do the lethal injection because of that little oath weirdness, so I guess they could be trained to do this fairly easily, not like getting a PharmD doesn't require lots of medical knowledge.

More interesting, to me anyways, is why they make the doctor go a month before brain wiping him. Doesn't seem to be any benefit to waiting that long, and if they did it weekly, so his first day was her first day, the doctors wouldn't have that "the first day is always the worst" problem.

Or at least do this, give them that month vacation, and then give them this duty again in 4 months after they come back — so every 6 months the same doctor is back to this shit assignment. You'd need six doctors for that cycle to work, and I am sure that with the entire world's population up for grabs, they can find six doctors who fit the bill.

In short, this is needlessly cruel on their own staff for no reason. But then, maybe "the Foundation is cold, not cruel" wasn't the motto yet when this was written.

(And I got way off topic for the comment I'm replying to, sorry about that!)

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Fuck is this brilliant.
Seriously. This should totally be on the Electronic Shadows thingy. … I don't think it even needs the text of SCP-231 to be understood.

Two notes.
1) This actually explains where all the wildly implausible containment breaches and such stories come from. They are the amnestic-induced memories of people that have been assigned to duties which'd fuck them up if they remembered.

2) Hippocratic oath is not important. The issue, why they keep sending him there over and over is, that he's one of the few people that can last through the duty without ending up like Decency.
The fact he was a mob doctor sort of points out what they were selecting by - folks who aren't entirely that principled, because as the saying goes, a shoot bends but a stick of wood breaks.
